en: Kṣemarāja: *Bodhavilāsa*.
Oṃ, salutation to Netra.
Salutations eternally to Śiva, the performer of the fivefold cosmic acts, who illumines the ultimate reality of one's own self as a mass of consciousness and bliss. // 1 //
Consciousness is declared to be the independent cause of the universe;
being the nature of autonomy and the knower, she bestows the supernatural powers.
On her own wall, for the sake of unfolding the universe by her own will,
she [manifests] through the diversity of various forms and the distinction between the grasped and the grasper.
The diversity of that universe is established through the distinction of objects of perception, by means of various diversities, and according to the enumeration of superior and inferior states. (4)
Through the contraction of consciousness, the conscious Maheśvara also [becomes limited];
they know that [state] there to be the universal form (viśvarūpa), like the banyan seed.
Consciousness is the nature of the self, pure and utterly stainless; that very same [consciousness], when attached to mental restraints, is designated as "citta. (6)
Consciousness, by being oriented toward objects, comes to rest in the mind;
because it is dominated by its own contraction, the wise know consciousness to be the mind.

The subject of illusion, whose nature is consciousness, exists for embodied beings as being identical with that [consciousness], yet remains attached to sense objects and devoid of true discernment. // 8 //
The mind is always one and constant, yet it appears as thirty-six principles through its divisions into parts, sentient beings, qualities, and so forth, by way of the seven types of subjects.
The one who is omnipresent, pure, and whose nature is perfect awakening is Maheśvara; through the thorough knowledge of Him as the "I," liberation rests in the palm of one's hand. // 10 //
When that Great Lord is meditated upon through the sevenfold subjectivity and the enumeration of the thirty-six principles, the Fortune of Liberation proceeds forth.
All those stages, such as the stage of seeing and so forth, undoubtedly belong to that [same] level;
just as an actor assumes various roles at will. (12)
In exactly the same way, the Self, expanded by the surging of its own will, consciousness, and bliss, assumes vast manifestations such as sight and the rest. (12)
The Self, radiant with the blossoming of the expansion of consciousness-bliss, shines forth;
yet, through the contraction of its own power, it becomes defiled within saṃsāra like a gem [obscured by dust]. // 13 //
"Though all-pervasive and the lord of the universe, he is defiled by various impurities—namely those called māyīya, āṇava, and kārmika—and thus thinks, 'I am incomplete. (15)
Just as the all-pervading Mahādeva performs the fivefold function, even so this Self, deluded by its powers (śakti), performs them likewise. (16)

When capable of expansion, he is praised by the proponents of reality as the Lord of Power (Śaktīśa); when contracted through contraction, he is designated as the transmigrating soul (saṃsārī). // 17 //

Indeed, when Māyā is intent on perceiving whatever form [exists], she should understand it as the creation of the object to be accomplished; the other power is considered to be persistence (sthiti). 18.
Through withdrawal, the Goddess is withdrawn; in the state of oneness with consciousness, she is considered to be grace (*anugraha*).
Because her essence alone does not manifest, it is designated as concealment (*tirodhāna*). (19)
Thus, this method of the fivefold flow is always present;
when known, it is a wish-fulfilling gem, but through ignorance, it is like a mere piece of wood or a clod of earth. (20)
He who constantly practices in this way by the power of true discernment shall be liberated from all bonds and become composed of eternal bliss. // 21 //
When this fire of consciousness, being fully awakened, devours [all objects], then that fire of consciousness should be known as stainless and all-devouring. // 22 //
Endowed with this power, the yogi, whose nature is nirvāṇa, attains the stainless state before long; there is no doubt about this. (23)
Even upon the attainment of power, the fire of consciousness shines as the universe consisting of pure consciousness;
this surges forth externally as waves of the nectar of its own bliss. (24)
That very [Self], having attained a state of fluidity, is perceived as the forms of existing things;
the Great Lord, the divine Maheśvara, the Supreme Sovereign, sports with his own self. 25.
Thus, he who knows this constantly is liberated and also liberates the multitude of beings in an instant from the terrible bondage of saṃsāra. (26)
Whoever possesses the power of bliss is established in the state of their own true nature; this is so for one whose arising is characterized by an ever-increasing surge of creative manifestation.
Even during the state of emergence, that which abides in its own essential nature is sought after;
this is realized by people precisely through the power of their effort. (28)
And from the expansion of the central channel, [the reality] shines forth from consciousness-bliss;
from that radiance, divine vision, which is of the nature of knowledge, is manifested. (29)
Stainless, radiant, pure, consisting of eternal bliss, and supreme—
even though it is free from the web of bodily fragmentation— the vision of gnosis unfolds.

But when the central channel expands, the means for its stabilization is powerful; it consists of many methods, such as the destruction of conceptual thought and the contraction and expansion [of the mind]. (31)
Through the mere non-thinking of anything, the destruction of conceptual constructions occurs;
she, whose power flashes forth from the awakening of consciousness, is attached to the circle of phenomena.
Attached to that, she beholds the stainless stream of the divine;
for this is called the contraction of power by the exponents of Brahman.
Likewise, there are the points of rest at the initial and final limits, as well as the dissolution of sound (nāda);
and the embracing of fearlessness, fear, anger, the loathsome, and so forth. // 34 //
Thus, O Goddess, has been described this which causes the expansion of the central abode;
by means of this, a capable person attains supreme perfection in just a few days. (35)
He who revolves within the internal formation of meditative concentration, possessing stainless luster,
does so by the power of emission alone, having reflected upon it again and again.
For even during emergence, the true nature of that yogin— who is established in awakening and whose essence is the flavor of eternal bliss— is clearly manifest.

For the practitioner intent on the internal efflorescence, that [consciousness] consists of light and bliss, is augmented by the potency of mantra, and is the fullness of the "I-consciousness" (pūrṇāhaṃtā). 38.
There, that radiant yogin, established in the state of a Lord of Mantras,
plays like the omnipresent Śakti, empowered by his own powers.
Thus, the sovereignty of that all-pervading Lord of the universe—
who assumes manifold distinctions and abides in variegated states— is unimpaired.
This is called non-duality, the unsurpassed nectar of knowledge; whoever drinks it, the swooning from the poison of saṃsāra is pacified for them. (41)
This extremely pure scripture is for the purpose of bestowing the splendor of awakening upon great souls so that they may attain Śiva; it belongs to the king named Kṣema.
Thus ends the Yoga Treatise entitled *Bodhavilāsa*, composed by the illustrious Kṣemarāja.
